title: Canonical constant-coefficient derived projection morphism
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme with small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Use $D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], $D(\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The constant-presheaf functor to presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules has the uniquely determined monoidal core whose unit and tensor constraints have identity components at every site object. Its composite with monoidal sheafification is the constant-sheaf functor $a^*$ of [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. It preserves flat objects. Let $L=La^*$, canonically identified with the termwise constant-complex functor since $a^*$ is exact, and let $R=R\Gamma(X_{\Et},-)$ be the unbounded right derived functor of [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor]. Use the canonical derived adjunction $L\dashv R$ induced from constant sheaves and global sections, with counit $\varepsilon$. The canonical comparison $c_{M,N}:L(M\otimes^L_\Lambda N)\longrightarrow LM\otimes^L_\Lambda LN$ is obtained by deriving the normalized ordinary constant-sheaf comonoidal constraint; on K-flat representatives it is the ordinary tensor comparison followed by the localization identifications. For arbitrary $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $K\in D(\Lambda)$ define the constant-coefficient projection morphism to be the adjunct of $c_{RE,K}$ followed by $\varepsilon_E\otimes 1_{LK}$:
$$\mathrm{PF}_{X,\Lambda}(E,K): RE\otimes^L_\Lambda K\longrightarrow R(E\otimes^L_\Lambda LK).$$
No finite dimension, torsion, boundedness, properness or invertibility assumption enters this construction.

The default CoreMonoidal coherence proofs verify naturality, associativity, and units componentwise, as in the existing Functor.Monoidal.const construction. Both prescribed hom-component identities hold by reflexivity.

For a flat coefficient module M, apply the existing geometric-fiber flatness criterion to its constant sheaf. At each separably closed geometric point s, Point.sheafFiberConstantSheafIso for (Scheme.pointSmallEtale s).ulift identifies its fiber with M. Transport ObjectProperty.flat along the inverse isomorphism. This also covers the empty scheme since the geometric-point condition is then vacuous.

The remaining constructions retain the normalized monoidal constant-presheaf functor, monoidal sheafification, and derived constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction. Introduce cachedDerivedTensorComparison with the existing leftDerivedTensorComparison verbatim as its data and no_expose, and prove cachedDerivedTensorComparison_eq by unfolding that interface. Retain the existing constantDerivedProjectionMap body using the cached comparison. The equation identifies the resulting mate with the former canonical mate exactly, while preventing kernel checking of applications from expanding the localization construction. The signature and mathematical morphism are unchanged. Compose the normalized monoidal constant-presheaf functor with monoidal sheafification, derive the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction, and take rightAdjointProjectionMap of the existing cachedDerivedTensorComparison. Package this same transformation with its inferred native type. The existing component definition is retained verbatim, and its equation with the named transformation is reflexive. Define the normalized source and target functors by tensor and composition; their equations with the native functors are reflexive. Thus the value of the existing map and all existing signatures remain unchanged. Use the inherited abelian additive and zero structures consistently and cache the existing sheaf tensor additivity as a theorem; the instance choices are definitionally equal to the standard ones. Name the existing derived constant functor by its defining expression, fixing its resolved instance data; the target functor uses this named functor. Its value remains the original leftDerivedFunctor.

Equip the derived constant functor with the shift structure transported along its canonical isomorphism to the exact termwise mapDerivedCategory functor. Transport triangulated exactness along this isomorphism. Derived global sections has its existing right-derived shift and triangulated structures. Tensoring is triangulated in either variable. Compose these structures to obtain the specified source and target shift structures and their exactness proofs. These are auxiliary functor structures and do not change the canonical projection map.
